report.headline: Well & Truly Cheese & Jalapeño Thins: strong packaging and product appeal, but distribution is the critical bottleneck; price is a secondary barrier.
key_findings: Distribution is the dominant constraint: 98.4% of all simulated agents (1,968 of 2,000) cited no stocking store anywhere along their week, and every never-exposed interview outside Kingston upon Thames confirms the product is effectively a Kingston-only trial.

Simulated conversion is concentrated in Kingston upon Thames: 5 of 13 interested agents bought (0.122 conversion), while all other top and bottom segments show near-zero or zero conversion, largely due to no store nearby.

Price is a clear secondary barrier: 5 agents (0.2% of all) rejected on price, with multiple quotes citing £2.80 versus a ~£1.80 usual snack price; this is a real friction but far smaller than distribution.

Packaging salience (4/5) works: 28 of 32 exposed agents noticed the product, and quotes repeatedly mention the packet standing out; however, 4 agents still did not notice it, suggesting shelf placement and visibility in convenience stores can be improved.

Need timing and loyalty are minor factors: 10 agents (0.5%) said the product was stocked where they live but not where they were when they needed it, and 3 (0.1%) stayed loyal to existing brands; these are secondary to availability.

rejection_reasons.title: No stocking store nearby
rejection_reasons.detail: 1,968 agents (98.4%) never encountered the product because no store along their routine stocked it. This is the overwhelming cause of non-purchase and explains zero conversion in Hammersmith and Fulham, Richmond upon Thames, and Kensington and Chelsea, as well as most never-exposed interviews across outer London boroughs.

rejection_reasons.title: Too expensive
rejection_reasons.detail: 5 agents (0.2% of all) rejected on price, with quotes comparing £2.80 per 100g to a usual ~£1.80 snack. This is a meaningful friction among those who did see it, but it is dwarfed by distribution; price-led promotions should be tested only where the product is actually stocked.

rejection_reasons.title: Stocked where they live, not where they are when needed
rejection_reasons.detail: 10 agents (0.5%) saw the product but could not buy it at the moment of need, typically at work or during commutes outside Kingston. This points to a need for placement in commuter and workplace-adjacent convenience stores, not just residential ones.

rejection_reasons.title: Did not notice on shelf
rejection_reasons.detail: 4 agents (0.2%) walked past the product without noticing it, despite high packaging salience. This suggests in-store visibility (shelf position, secondary displays) can be improved, though the small count limits strong conclusions.

rejection_reasons.title: Loyal to existing brand
rejection_reasons.detail: 3 agents (0.1%) stayed with their usual brand. This is a minor barrier and likely reflects habit and price sensitivity rather than a product flaw.

interested_segments.title: Kingston upon Thames residents (all archetypes)
interested_segments.detail: 41 agents in Kingston, 13 interested, 5 bought (12.2% conversion). This is the only segment with meaningful simulated conversion and should be the focus of initial expansion and marketing. Interviews show purchases at Co-op, Tesco Express, Shell Select, Food Fare, Evergreens, and Londis, indicating convenience and supermarket formats work when stocked.

interested_segments.title: Shift workers
interested_segments.detail: 112 agents, 1 interested, 1 bought (0.89% conversion). The single buyer cited high protein and gluten-free as purchase drivers, suggesting a niche opportunity if the product is placed in convenience stores near shift-worker routes. However, the small interested count means this is a weak signal, not a proven segment.

interested_segments.title: Students
interested_segments.detail: 158 agents, 2 interested, 1 bought (0.63% conversion). Students noticed the packaging and liked the jalapeño kick, but price sensitivity and low need limited conversion. Any student-focused push should be paired with a lower price point or multipack value.

action_items.action: Prioritise distribution expansion beyond Kingston upon Thames, starting with convenience and supermarket stores in adjacent boroughs such as Richmond upon Thames, Hammersmith and Fulham, and Merton.
action_items.rationale: 98.4% of agents cited no stocking store nearby, and zero conversion in nearby boroughs is almost entirely due to lack of availability. Expanding to adjacent boroughs with similar demographics is the highest-leverage move.

action_items.action: Within Kingston, secure placement in commuter and workplace-adjacent convenience stores (e.g., near Kingston station, bus routes, and university campuses) in addition to residential stores.
action_items.rationale: 10 agents (0.5%) said the product was stocked where they live but not where they were when they needed it; quotes mention work and commute moments. Kingston already has 12.2% conversion, so improving need-moment availability can lift sales further.

action_items.action: Test a price promotion or smaller pack size in Kingston stores to address the £2.80 vs ~£1.80 price gap, and monitor conversion among price-sensitive segments such as students and low-income shoppers.
action_items.rationale: Price was the second most cited rejection reason (5 agents, 0.2%), and multiple quotes explicitly compared £2.80 to a ~£1.80 usual snack. A targeted test can clarify whether price is a real barrier or a secondary excuse.

action_items.action: Improve in-store visibility in stocked Kingston stores through shelf talkers, secondary displays, or eye-level placement, and track whether did-not-notice rates fall.
action_items.rationale: 4 agents (0.2%) did not notice the product despite high packaging salience (4/5). While small, this suggests shelf execution can be tightened, especially in convenience stores where shoppers scan quickly.

action_items.action: Use Instagram and TikTok content to drive trial in Kingston, focusing on the jalapeño kick and high-protein/gluten-free benefits, and include store locator links for Kingston stockists.
action_items.rationale: Marketing intensity is currently low (0.3), and interviews show some buyers had seen online content. Social channels can amplify the strong packaging and product story, but only where the product is actually available.
